events.title: Sputnik 2 Launches Laika into Orbit
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2, carrying Laika, a stray dog from Moscow, making her the first animal to orbit the Earth. Laika died in orbit within hours from overheating and stress, though this was not publicly disclosed for decades.
events.significance: It demonstrated that a living organism could survive launch and weightlessness, paving the way for human spaceflight, while also raising ethical debates about animal testing in space research.

events.title: Panama Declares Independence from Colombia
events.description: Panama proclaimed its separation from Colombia with the backing of the United States, whose warships prevented Colombian forces from suppressing the uprising. The U.S. recognized the new republic within days.
events.significance: The secession cleared the way for the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty and the construction of the Panama Canal, which transformed global maritime trade and established U.S. influence in the region.

events.title: Washington, D.C. Residents Vote in a Presidential Election
events.description: In the U.S. presidential election, Lyndon B. Johnson won in a landslide over Barry Goldwater. It was also the first presidential election in which residents of Washington, D.C. could vote, following ratification of the 23rd Amendment in 1961.
events.significance: Johnson's victory gave him a strong mandate for his Great Society programs, and the election extended presidential voting rights to D.C. residents for the first time.

events.title: Columbus Sights Dominica
events.description: On his second voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus sighted an island in the Lesser Antilles on a Sunday and named it Dominica, from the Latin for Sunday.
events.significance: The landfall marked the start of expanded European exploration and colonization of the Caribbean, with profound consequences for the Indigenous peoples of the region.

events.title: Kiel Mutiny Begins
events.description: German sailors at Kiel mutinied when ordered to sail on a final, hopeless naval operation against the British. The revolt spread rapidly to other ports and cities across Germany.
events.significance: The mutiny sparked the German Revolution of 1918-1919, contributed to the abdication of Kaiser Wilhelm II, and hastened the end of World War I and the founding of the Weimar Republic.
